Set A has no yahooquery/Yahoo cross-check anywhere in its spec or architecture, and never uses the user's 10-name delisted list. Its replacement is a UNIV-04 check set the researcher collects from press releases. Set B drops the PPO trading/allocation agents from S4, calling them 'a separate, later idea'. It also contradicts the compute constraint: its spec lists 'Cloud compute; every model trains on the user's machine' as out of scope, and AD-23 says 'no cloud', even though the user rents GPUs now and then. Its brief also still reads as S1-only ('not in this first stage', 'What success looks like' covers data only). On quant soundness A is stronger. It has one walk-forward schedule with gaps and a lockbox, a hypothesis ledger whose every test runs through null-hypothesis-testing, parallel-analysis factor counts and a fitted Marchenko–Pastur edge, an LSTM and TFT-lite against baselines, PPO agents with per-line budgets, and GPU bundles with verified teardown. A also gives M1 real oracles: TC-01–TC-27 are synthetic known-answer cases with exact expected rows. B's qdata tests.md says 'No golden cases yet', so its M1 data correctness rests only on smoke tests and unit tests. B is better on milestone shape: each stage starts with a skeleton milestone (M4 study skeleton, M6 feature skeleton, M8 forecast skeleton), and M1 already delivers the live WebSocket run monitor and the company and universe pages. A's M1 shows only a membership page, and A's M4 openly skips the S2 skeleton. B also ships CONSTRAINTS.md with a no-import-from-references rule. A refers to CONSTRAINTS.md in AGENTS.md and in every packet, but the file is missing. A's packets were tighter and complete in the samples I read. B's mount_reads packet leaves out the route paths and the query.Bars/Returns/Actions types. B's plan also labels several 'spine' tasks as Kind thicken / Mode split with a 'fold' reason, which is confusing. Weighing these, A wins narrowly on research depth and the S2–S4 design, and B is ahead on how S1 is delivered and on structure.
